items.title: Hamas agrees to disarmament roadmap under Gaza ceasefire deal
items.description: The Palestinian militant group said it had accepted a US-backed plan under which its weapons would be transferred to a new Palestinian governing body as Israeli forces withdraw in phases, though Israel has yet to endorse the agreement and insists any pullback depends on Hamas's complete disarmament.

items.title: Boldly going in different directions? US and Russia diverge on joint space plans.
items.description: U.S.-Russia space cooperation, a success story of the Cold War, could be under threat if a new agreement can't be reached.

items.title: Hamas agrees to disarm under Trump ceasefire deal
items.description: Hamas said on Friday it had agreed to hand over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee as part of a US-backed roadmap that would see a gradual Israeli military withdrawal from Gaza, though Israel said it would not pull back until the militant group is fully disarmed.

items.title: Middle East: Civilian death toll climbs in Gaza, Lebanon and West Bank as UN chief demands ‘the fighting must stop’
items.description: Violence and civilian casualties are rising across the Middle East – from Israeli airstrikes in Gaza to continued hostilities in Lebanon and the West Bank – UN agencies reported on Friday as the Secretary-General declared “the fighting must stop”.

items.title: Military flare-up between Houthis and Saudi Arabia challenges relative calm in Yemen
items.description: Riyadh and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are on the brink of renewed conflict. Could war-ravaged Yemen be drawn into a wider Middle East war?

items.title: Trump announces deal for Hamas to disarm, militants demand Israel withdraws from Gaza first
items.description: President Trump announced that his Board of Peace has reached a deal with Hamas to completely disarm, calling it a "historic breakthrough." But a senior Hamas official says Israel must withdraw first.

items.title: Writing on Wall for Putin in D.C.
items.description: Timothy Ash argues that Washington’s growing bipartisan support for tougher Russia sanctions, Ukraine’s battlefield gains and drone warfare edge are shifting the dynamics of the war. He says mounting pressure could push Vladimir Putin toward negotiations as the Kremlin faces rising economic and military challenges.
